inc.text: Cyprus Post confirmed a cyberattack; screenshots of mail addressed to the Presidential Palace, ministries and embassies appeared on the dark web. The post office says the central database was not reached.

inc.text: The health service of Extremadura detected a breach of its online health-centre app on 5 October: clinical information of 18,416 users was compromised. Police arrested the suspected attacker on 29 October.

inc.text: The ShinyHunters group named Icelandic schools, among them the University of Iceland and Reykjavik University, as victims of its attack on the learning platform Canvas; no leak of Icelandic data is confirmed.

inc.label: 19 Nov 2026
inc.text: European Commission (EU institution in Brussels): a Commission spokesperson confirmed on 19 November an "AI-generated cyber campaign", first detected on 22 October. Several internal staff services were taken offline as a precaution for more than ten days, including the Sysper HR platform, payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements and translation. The Commission says it has notified affected people, found no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole and knows of no ransom demand; the investigation is still open. It did not name the tool or the attackers. Politico reported that CERT-EU identified the open-source AI hacking tool ARTEX; the Commission has not confirmed this. Nobody has been named. It is the Commission's third disclosed cyber incident in 2026, after Ivanti software in January and its cloud in March; officials have not linked them.

inc.label: 18 Nov 2026
inc.text: Bulgaria's digital transformation minister Ivan Vasilev said on 18 November that intruders had been inside government document-exchange systems since 2021 and had taken more than 130 GB of data, about 62 million pages. A new national monitoring system detected the activity in August 2026, and prosecutors were told to examine how state bodies acted while it went unnoticed. He said several international hacking groups are believed involved, with no conclusive link to a foreign state, and no evidence so far that citizens' personal data was compromised.

inc.label: 17 Nov 2026
inc.text: Equinor said on 17 November that it had detected an ongoing cyberattack on certain IT systems, with operations and production not affected and no sign of data theft. On 19 November it said the attack was still ongoing, did not appear to target Equinor specifically, and had been reported to the police. On 20 November it said the attack had been stopped, with production normal and no sign that data was stolen or altered. Norway's National Security Authority is assisting. The kind of attack has not been disclosed and nobody has been named.

inc.label: 18 Nov 2026
inc.text: Skagerak Energi, a Norwegian power company, said on 18 November that outsiders had broken into some of its IT systems. It says operations and production were not affected and there is no sign of information leaking; it informed the energy regulator NVE, KraftCERT and the National Security Authority, but not the police. It came one day after the Equinor attack; whether the two are linked is not known. Nobody has been named.

inc.label: 16 Nov 2026
inc.text: Lithuanian Customs said it identified a cyber incident on 10 November and shut down its Common User Management Portal (BAP), which also gives access to EU customs platforms such as ICS2. Acting customs chief Vygantas Paigozinas called it a deliberate attack and said data of possibly several hundred individuals and companies may have been affected. On 16 November customs said some services had reopened via the national e-government portal; no attacker has been named.

inc.label: 14 Nov 2026
inc.text: La Poste announced on 14 November that a cyberattack on its subsidiary Maileva, which sends mail for corporate clients, exposed the first names, surnames and postal addresses of 22 million people who receive mail from Maileva's business customers. Reports date the intrusion to mid-September. Maileva told the data regulator CNIL, and the Paris prosecutor's cybercrime section opened an investigation. The perpetrators have not been identified.

inc.label: 18 Nov 2026
inc.text: The French EV-charging platform Chargemap told users on 18 November (reported by VRT NWS) that attackers got in on 8 November through a flaw in an old technical interface, which it closed on 12 November. Stolen data includes e-mail addresses, names, places of residence, dates of birth and phone numbers; the company says payment details were not taken and passwords were not leaked in readable form. The number of affected accounts is unknown; the company notified the regulator CNIL.

inc.label: 18 Nov 2026
inc.text: Ireland's credit-union minister Robert Troy told RTE on 18 November that about 40 of the country's 160 credit unions were affected by an October attack on their online-banking software provider, Wellington IT, which told them only in mid-November. Saved payee details (names, account numbers, addresses) may have been accessed; reports say passwords, PINs and card details were not affected. Wellington IT says it lacks logs to tell which records were taken and treats all as potentially affected.

Austria: The Interior Ministry counted 111 ransomware cases in Austria in 2025.
Bulgaria: The state IT company said it repelled an attack of more than 400 gigabits per second on the national health information system (date not found).
The police cybercrime chief says a Bulgarian company falls victim to ransomware almost every month.
Croatia: The national response team recorded 1,203 incidents in the first nine months of 2026: 439 were phishing, three were ransomware.
In November 2026 it said it had recorded no attack on refrigeration systems in Croatia.
Cyprus: The Bank of Cyprus Oncology Centre confirmed that patient and staff data taken from its systems was published (date not found).
Czechia: Of the 203 incidents in 2025, 12 were rated significant and two very significant.
Denmark: A public tracker counts 97 known data leaks in Denmark in 2026 up to 26 October, more than in any earlier year.

Also reported, date not found: patient data leaked from a chain of GP practices; names and addresses of up to 400,000 customers of telecom operator 3 reached; a hack at Aarhus University with no sign that sensitive data leaked.
The authorities rate the threat from cybercrime and cyber-espionage against Denmark as "very high".
Finland: Ransomware reports to the national cyber centre rose in summer 2026; small firms were hit most, through flaws that were not repaired or logins without a second step.
51% of reported Microsoft 365 account takeovers in 2026 used one specific phishing trick (device codes).
Malware cases reported to the national cyber centre rose about 28% in 2025; the most common ransomware was Akira.
In September 2026 breach reports were 81.5% higher than the month before.
France: The data-protection authority received 5,629 breach notifications in 2025, 20% more than in 2024.
Germany: A private chronicle counts 356 ransomware incidents in Germany in 2026 up to 10 November.
Greece: A security firm counted 1,928 attacks per organisation per week in Greece in October 2026, 26% more than a year earlier.
Hungary: In the State Treasury attack (August 2026) attackers reached pension and family-support systems and municipal account data; a group offered the data for sale.
Italy: 148 confirmed ransomware attacks in Italy in the first half of 2026 (industry count); attacks on hospitals rose 20% in 2025.
The national cyber agency counted 3,271 cyber events in the first nine months of 2026, more than the 2,729 of all 2025; 1,922 had a confirmed impact.
Ransomware attacks counted by the agency: 91 in the first half of 2025 and 54 in the second half.
Latvia: Second quarter of 2026: 673 incidents handled by hand, 20% fewer than the quarter before; ransomware and data leaks did the most damage.
Lithuania: First nine months of 2026: 1,172 incidents, 52% fewer than in the same period of 2025.
The national centre found more than 106,000 leaked logins and warned 221 organisations.
The national centre recorded 2,888 incidents in 2025, 25% fewer than in 2024.
In the registers case the thieves logged in with accounts of Migration Department staff; prosecutors put the damage at no less than €111,000.
Luxembourg: Also reported, date not found: a major attack on a firm that hosts health data for doctors' practices.
Poland: Ransomware in health care: 13 incidents so far in 2026 against 10 in all of 2025 (the national e-health centre).
Also reported: a leak at a medical software platform covering close to 19 million people; investigators said in February 2026 they had identified who was behind it.
Portugal: A security firm counted 2,639 attacks per organisation per week in June 2026, 29% more than a year earlier.
Romania: Land registry attack (July 2026): about 100 of 1,083 virtual servers were deleted, the servers had no antivirus, and the first entry was through a login page exposed to the internet (national cyber directorate).
Spain: Leak-site trackers list 533 Spanish ransomware victims.
Estonia: Incidents with an impact: 6,515 in 2024 and a record 10,185 in 2025, mostly fraud and phishing.
Slovenia: In the state administration breach (late October 2026), 7,216 of the 15,000 records contained scrambled passwords.
Liechtenstein: After the register breach four state systems were taken offline; the way in was the portal used to file entries in the register. No sign that vital infrastructure was affected.
